note: The starter library a new team gets. FORMATIONS, NOT PLAYS: alignment and labels only — no routes, no jobs, no target, no names, no club. A coach draws his own football on top, and what he draws is his. Every entry is a set of parameters, not a set of coordinates; nothing here was lifted from anybody's playbook. Slugs are prefixed fm- so a starter formation can never collide with a play already in a book.
units: Distances are yards. Depth is measured from the line named in lineLabel; width is measured from the ball (or from the kicker on a free kick). See formations.js for the two draw scales and why a line split is not drawn to scale.

formations.name: Punt — Spread
formations.note: The standard. One-yard splits, gunners at the numbers, punter at fourteen. Seven on the line: five interior plus the two gunners, which is what leaves the wings free to be off it.

formations.name: Punt — Tight
formations.note: Same eleven, everything pulled in: foot splits, gunners in tight, punter a yard shallower. For a wet ball, a short field, or a young snapper.

formations.name: Punt — Spread, left hash
formations.note: The same punt with the ball on the left hash: the boundary gunner has less room, so his split comes in. Proof the ball spot is a parameter and not baked into the drawing.

formations.name: Punt Return — 6-2-2-1
formations.note: Six up front, two jammers of them on the gunners; two at the second level, two building the wall, one returner at forty.

formations.name: Punt Return — 5-2-3-1
formations.note: One fewer up front and a three-man wall. Less pressure on the punter, more men building the return.

formations.name: Kickoff — Spread 5/5
formations.note: Ten across, five either side of the kicker, evenly laddered from four yards out to twenty-four. A free kick needs four either side of the kicker and this has five.

formations.name: Kickoff — Cluster
formations.note: Everybody inside the numbers in staggered pairs, then they break for their lanes on the whistle. The stagger is football, not drawing: men leaving a bunch at different times cannot start on the same line.

formations.name: Kickoff — Onside 6/4
formations.note: Overload the kick side: six bunched right in two ranks, four spread left to cover the other half if it gets away. Where the ball is put is the coach's call, not the formation's.

formations.name: Kick Return — 5-2-2-2
formations.note: Five across as the hands team on the ten-yard line, two at the second level, two in the wall, two deep. Nobody inside the free kick zone.

formations.name: Kick Return — 5-4-2
formations.note: Same hands team and the same deep pair; the four blockers align on one row instead of in two pairs, which builds the wall sooner and gives up the second level.

formations.name: Offense — 2x2, tight end right
formations.note: Two receivers each side counting the tight end, quarterback at five, one back. Seven on the line is solved for, not assumed: five linemen, the tight end, and the backside X.

formations.name: Offense — Trips right
formations.note: No tight end, three receivers right, single receiver left. Two of the four have to be on the line to make seven, and the generator puts them where a legal trips set puts them: the outermost man on each side.

formations.name: Offense — Tight, two backs
formations.note: Tight end right, one receiver each side, two backs behind the quarterback. The heavy end of the same generator: only the numbers changed.

formations.name: Defense — 4-3
formations.note: Four down, three backers, two corners, two safeties. There is no seven-on-the-line rule for the defence; what is checked is that four men are actually down on the ball.

formations.name: Defense — 5-2
formations.note: The youth staple: a nose on the centre, five down, two backers behind them. Hard to run inside on, and it asks less of eleven- to fourteen-year-olds than reading a gap.

formations.name: Defense — 4-4
formations.note: Four down, four backers, one free safety. Eight in the box against a team that only runs.
